$comment: Generated from the xeo-*.ttl modules by tools/gen_profile.py — do not edit by hand.

conventions.label: the class local name, PascalCase
conventions.propertyKey: the datatype property local name, camelCase
conventions.relationshipType: UPPER_SNAKE of the object property local name

ActionItem.definition: Something a person or a team was understood to have agreed to do, read from a meeting or a message: where it was raised (raisedIn), who is to do it (assignedTo), and what, in plain language (name). An interpretation, because it is a reading of what was agreed; one a model extracted carries method and producedByModel (core). Not a WorkItem (work): an action item is what was agreed, a work item is a step someone has taken on.

AgentRuntime.definition: The product that runs the agent loop and loads a harness (Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, OpenCode). Identified by name with runtimeVersion: one node per version. Not a library for building agents, and not a harness: the runtime is the vendor's program, the harness is what is loaded into it.

AgentSession.definition: One continuous run of an AgentRuntime under one Harness, from its start to its end: immutable once ended. Identified by sessionRef. Carries startedAt, endedAt, startType, underHarness and onRuntime, and its turns (hasTurn). A resumed session keeps its sessionRef; a session begun after a clear or a handoff is a new one, which points at the old with continuesSession. High-volume: the column store keeps the rows of its calls, the graph keeps the session and what is traversed from it.

AgentTurn.definition: All the work one prompt set off within a session: the model calls (hasModelCall) and tool calls (hasToolCall) between one prompt and the next. Identified by turnRef. A turn here is one prompt's worth of work; a framework that calls each pass of the model loop a turn is describing a ModelCall.

AlgorithmRun.definition: One execution of one algorithm over one projection of the graph at a time: immutable once finished. Carries algorithm (which method), parameters (as run), projection (what it ran on) and ranAt. The provenance record for every score and derived edge it wrote: outputs point back with computedBy, or name the run in their method. Re-running with a different projection or parameters is a new run, never an update to an old one.

AnswerEngine.definition: An assistant that answers a person in its own interface, with or without web search and citations: ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude, and multi-turn agents and voice surfaces acting for a user (ConversationalAgent until 0.7). The AEO surface.

Arm.definition: One version in an Experiment: the A or the B. A named condition that differs from the baseline in what it changes (testsTactic), or is the baseline itself (isBaseline). Identified by its Experiment (hasArm) and its name. Its trials are hasTrial. Its own figures on the experiment's primaryMetric, computed over those trials, are armMean, armStandardDeviation and armSampleSize.

AttributedCredit.definition: One touch's credit for one conversion under one model: creditedTouchpoint, creditFor, usesAttributionModel, creditShare, and attributedRevenue and attributedConversions where they apply. The credits of one conversion under one model sum to 1 (or, for full_credit_each, each is 1).

AttributionModel.definition: A rule for giving conversions' credit to touches, described by its structure, not its name: creditRule, its CreditAnchors (positions and weights), lookbackWindow, the touch types eligible, deduplicationRule, dateBasis and revenueBasis. Vendor names such as 'U-shaped' are mapped in mappings/, not trusted: two vendors' U-shaped can put the remaining credit on different touches. A rule, so a norm; a changed rule is a new AttributionModel.

AttributionRollup.definition: Credited totals for one channel, campaign, ad set or ad over one window under one model: attributedRevenue and attributedConversions, with periodStart, periodEnd, usesAttributionModel and method. A MetricReading of an attribution Metric. The graph keeps rollups; the per-touch credits may live in the column store.

Benchmark.definition: A fixed set of test tasks plus a way to grade them. A public model benchmark counts, and so does a team's own set of twenty SEO audit tasks. Identified by name with benchmarkVersion: changing a task or the grading makes a new version. graderKind says how its tasks are scored.

BenchmarkTask.definition: One task inside one version of a Benchmark (inBenchmark), identified there by its taskRef. A Trial runs an arm on one task (onTask).

BookedMeeting.definition: A meeting booked through a scheduler or by a salesperson: a kind of ConversionEvent. Its outcome (held, no-show) is callOutcome.

Brand.definition: A named market identity that engines may mention, cite, or recommend. Distinct from Website: a brand can be visible on the whole web, not only its own origin.

Call.definition: A phone call that happened: a kind of ConversionEvent, captured by a call-tracking system. Carries occurredAt and, once judged, callOutcome.

Campaign.definition: A body of work inside a Project, usually against one Topic: the URLs and Terms it covers and, where it is measured, the one Objective it is measured by. Recommendations are issuedFor a campaign, and it is the unit an operator plans a cycle around. A campaign need not have a Topic, an Objective, targets or a results window; a team that requires them checks them with the optional profile shapes/profiles/agency-delivery.ttl. Soft-deleted like its Project.

Capability.definition: A lever or strength a party can bring to bear (content, technical, PR, brand, ...). The unit of the scope gate: a Tactic is in reach only when every Capability it requires is approved. Specific capabilities are instances, not subclasses.

Chargeback.definition: A payment reversed by the buyer's bank against an Order (refundsOrder). Carries refundedAmount. Its grounding is provisional: chargeback records differ most between processors.

Claim.definition: A party's assertion about an effect: 'this tool saves 40% of tokens', 'FAQ markup doubles AI citations'. Never an observation, whoever makes it. Carries its words (statement), who made it (claimedBy), when (claimedAt) and where (claimSourceUri), and where it states a number, the claimedValue, the Metric it is a value of (claimMetric) and what it is compared against (counterfactual). Identified by claimant, statement and date. Whether it holds is a ClaimCheck.

ClaimCheck.definition: Our test of a Claim: the Claim it checks (checksClaim), the Experiment that ran (checkedBy) and the verdict (claimVerdict). An interpretation, because a verdict is a reading of an experiment against what was claimed. A claim may be checked more than once; each check is its own node.

Compaction.definition: The replacement of a session's conversation history by a summary, at a time. Carries compactionTrigger, occurredAt, inSession and, where the runtime reports them, tokensBefore and tokensAfter. Where the runtime keeps the summary it wrote, artifactUri (core) points at it: the summary is what the next turn loads.

Consent.definition: One recorded consent choice, for one purpose (consentPurpose), by one subject (consentSubject), as one system captured it (consentCapturedBy), with its status and when it was recorded. A new choice is a new Consent, never an edit; the current status for a subject and purpose is the latest. Company-level choices, such as not using a company's data to train models, sit on the Organization. Validity under any law is an interpretation made elsewhere, not part of this record.

ConversionEvent.definition: A submission/click/unlock that happened at a time: a visitor's action on a ConversionPoint, recorded by the capturing system. Immutable once recorded. Identified by the capturing system and its submission id; one per submission. Not the creation of a CRM record, which may follow, be merged into an existing record, or never happen: events are not leads.

ConversionPoint.definition: A durable on-page mechanism that turns attention into a pipeline event. Identified by the URL it sits on and its form id or selector. Its kind is conversionPointType.

Crawl.definition: One crawl run over one Website: time-bounded, agent-attributed, immutable once finished.

CreditAnchor.definition: One fixed position a position-based model gives a share to, and the share: anchorPosition and anchorWeight. A U-shaped model has two (first_touch 0.4, lead_created 0.4); the rest is spread by the model's rule.

Delegation.definition: A parent agent starting a subagent with its own context. Carries parentAgentId and childAgentId as the runtime reports them, occurredAt, the session it happened in (inSession) and, where the subagent ran as a session of its own, childSession. Carrying work from one session to the next is not a delegation: that is continuesSession.

Deliverable.definition: What was handed back for review, at a time, by a person or an agent: a change set, a document, a report. Carries occurredAt, the WorkItem it answers (fulfils) and artifactUri; where an agent made it, producedInSession (agentic) says in which session. Handing it back says nothing about whether it was accepted: that judgment is a review, which is not modelled yet. Not an Outcome, which is what was measured after the work shipped.

DesignAsset.definition: A file a design uses: a logo, an icon, an illustration, a photograph, a graphic, a font, a video (assetKind). Identified by where the file is kept (artifactUri, core); the graph holds the pointer, never the file. Used by components, patterns, templates, concepts and pages (usesAsset). Who may use it, and on what terms (licence, credit, expiry), is not a term yet: it waits until a project needs it, and will then follow schema.org.

DesignComponent.definition: A reusable piece of interface with a name and a defined anatomy: a button, a card, a header, a form field. Built from tokens (usesToken), smaller components (composedOf) and assets (usesAsset). A variant (the primary button of a button, the compact card of a card) is a component of its own that points at the one it varies (variantOf) and says what sets it apart (variantValue). Kept where it is defined, a design file or a code library (artifactUri, core); the component in the design file and the one in code are one DesignComponent where they are meant to match. Not an HTML element, and not a CMS block, though a block may implement one.

DesignConcept.definition: A rendered proposal for one piece of interface, usually under one DesignDirection: a card, a hero, a page, or a direction's version of an element of the existing site. Names what it depicts (depicts: a component, pattern, template, element or page) and the direction it was drawn under (underDirection); where it is offered in place of an element of the existing site, replacesElement names that element. Kept as an image, a design-file frame or a prototype (artifactUri, core); the tool's own id for that frame or page is its designRecordRef. Where a model drew it, method and producedByModel (core) say how. A card concept is a DesignConcept that depicts a card component. Not a skos:Concept, which is a code in a scheme.

DesignDecision.definition: A reviewer's call on one piece of a design proposal: keep, replace or remove an element of the existing site; approve, shortlist, send back for changes (revise) or reject a direction or a concept; or defer (designVerdict). Names what it decides on (decidesOn), who decided (decidedBy), when (occurredAt, core), and, where the call holds under one direction only, which (underDirection). A replacement may name the concept chosen (chosenConcept). The reviewer's reason in their own words is its statement (decision). An interpretation: a judgment of fit, labeled as one. A changed mind is a new decision beside the old one, never an edit of it. Not Feedback (decision), which judges a machine's claim about a gap or a recommendation.

DesignDirection.definition: One proposed visual approach for a site or a brand: a name, the idea behind it in words (statement, decision), and how it treats type, colour, imagery and layout, shown through the DesignConcepts drawn under it (underDirection). Several are usually proposed together, in one Deliverable (proposedIn, work), for one Website, Brand or Project (directionFor). A durable option that concepts and decisions point at. Whether it fits is a reviewer's call, kept as a DesignDecision about it, never as a flag on the direction. Its rank among the directions of a proposal is not a property either: a ranking is a judgment, kept as the DesignDecisions about each direction (shortlist, reject) with a statement. A design system built out of a chosen direction names it (fromDirection).

DesignElement.definition: One part of an existing site's design, catalogued so it can be reviewed: a logo treatment, a colour, a type style, a style of photography, a divider, the navigation, a recurring component (elementKind). Belongs to one Website (elementOf) and is seen on its pages (seenOn). Where the same thing is also catalogued in a design system, realizedAs names the token, component, pattern, template or asset. A redesign asks of each element whether to keep, replace or remove it, and under each direction with what: a DesignDecision, and the DesignConcepts that replace it (replacesElement).

DesignPattern.definition: A reusable answer to a recurring interface problem, made of components: a hero, a pricing table, a filtered listing, a sign-up flow. Larger than a component and smaller than a page; composedOf names the components and patterns it is made of. A pattern says how a problem is solved. Whether a page must use it is a Practice (decision), not a property of the pattern.

DesignSystem.definition: A named, versioned set of the decisions a brand's or a site's interfaces are built from: its tokens, components, patterns and page templates (each inDesignSystem), and the assets they use. Identified by name and designSystemVersion. Kept where it is maintained, a design file, a code library or a documentation site (artifactUri, core): the graph holds the pointer and the structure, never the files. A Website is built with one (usesDesignSystem). One built out of a proposed direction names it (fromDirection).

DesignToken.definition: One named design decision stored as a value, so design files and code share it: a colour, a spacing step, a font family, a duration, a shadow. Its name (core) is its path in the token file, such as color.brand.primary; its tokenType is one of the W3C Design Tokens Format's types; its tokenValue is the value as written there. A token that refers to another (an alias, {color.blue.500} in that format) names it with aliasOf and need carry no value of its own. tokenTier says whether it is a primitive, a semantic or a component token. A token whose value changes by mode (light and dark, one brand and another; Figma calls these modes) is one token per mode, each with its tokenMode; where the value depends on more than one axis (dark and mobile), one token per combination, with one tokenMode per axis. Belongs to one DesignSystem.

Diagnostic.definition: A named, reusable check or framework that reads observations and reveals gaps (e.g. a waterfall-position assessment). The framework is durable; each finding it produces is a Gap.

DiagnosticRun.definition: One execution of a Diagnostic against one scope at a time: immutable once finished, method-attributed. The Diagnostic is the durable check; the run is the occasion it was applied, and each Gap it found is revealedIn that run. Carries ranAt and websiteId. A later run supersedes an earlier one without deleting it, so a finding can always be traced to the data it was read from.

Domain.definition: A registrable domain (the public suffix plus one label, e.g. example.co.uk), identified by its name in lower case. The publisher-level identity a URL sits on, whether or not the site is under observation: a competitor's result has no partOf edge to a tracked Website, it has onDomain. Not tenant-scoped: one node per domain, shared by every tenant that sees it, and it carries no websiteId.

EnforcementEvent.definition: The record that a harness rule was evaluated at an enforcement point and returned a decision: a hook denied a tool call, a permission rule asked the user, a guard trimmed an output. Carries enforcementDecision, decisionSource, reasonText, occurredAt, inSession, the ToolCall it was about (onToolCall) and, where the rule is modelled, the Practice that fired (firedPractice). An episode, written by the enforcement point itself at the time. A rule judged afterwards to have applied is appliedPractice (decision), a derivation.

Engine.definition: A system that mediates between a person's question and web content. A parent class only: every engine node is one of its subtypes, SearchEngine (here), or GenerativeOverview or AnswerEngine (visibility).

Entity.definition: A real-world thing or concept that content is about — a product, a place, a person, a material, a method — identified by a reference into a public knowledge base (entityRef) where one exists, otherwise by name. Distinct from Topic, which is a site-scoped grouping somebody derived, and from Brand, which is a market identity engines mention: an Entity is the thing itself, shared across sites. Not tenant-scoped. Named for the knowledge-graph sense of the word; not to be confused with the layer 'entity', which Website, URL and Term also occupy.

Experiment.definition: A test of a tactic that ran over a time window: immutable once concluded, method-attributed. The precedent record the decision layer learns from.

ExternalEvent.definition: Something outside the work that happened at a time and could move the metrics an experiment reads: an engine's ranking update, a site migration, an outage, a seasonal peak, a competitor's launch. Carries name and occurredAt. An episode, recorded once and shared: whether it actually affected a given result is a separate claim, carried on confoundedBy.

Feedback.definition: An operator's judgment of a machine's claim, hung off whatever it judges (feedbackOn): a diagnosed Gap, or the Recommendation issued to close one. Carries a verdict (a slotted-in concept), a statement in the operator's words, and who gave it and when. Not a TacticAssessment, which is a scored estimate of an approach on one dimension: Feedback is a person agreeing or disagreeing with a claim about one case. Never deleted: a rejected finding and the reason it was rejected are what a Practice is later written from. A Practice promoted from a Feedback is authored (source): it stands on the operator's authority, and no experiment earned it. learned is kept for a rule earned from Experiments.

Framework.definition: A named method: a set of Stages, ordered or not, with the Diagnostics, Tactics and Practices hung on them. An optimization waterfall (ordered stages, each with a test, a subject placed at the first stage it fails), a tactic matrix, a launch checklist and a discipline playbook are all Frameworks, told apart by frameworkKind and never by subclass. A norm: it says how the work should be approached, it is authored and revisable, and it is identified by name within its author's scope. Distinct from Playbook, which is the unordered bundle a discipline reuses; a Framework adds the structure, and may include what a Playbook includes. The method is the instance you author. XEO ships the frame and none of the stages.

Gap.definition: A diagnosed deficit between current and desired visibility. First-order, but a claim: asserted by a Diagnostic from evidence, never observed directly. Its kind (gapType) is a slotted-in skos:Concept — e.g. a Citation-Waterfall stage — not a subclass baked into the ontology.

GenerativeOverview.definition: A search engine's generated answer on its own results page: Google's AI Overviews and AI Mode, Bing's generated answers. Tied to the SearchEngine it appears on (shownOnSearchEngine). The GEO surface. Was GenerativeEngine until 0.7.

Harness.definition: Everything around a model that makes it act as an agent: instructions, tool guidance, memory, skills, subagent definitions, hooks, plugins, scripts, permission rules, settings. A named, versioned bundle of HarnessComponents (hasComponent), written for an AgentRuntime (runsOn). It has two identities: name with harnessVersion, for people, and harnessDigest, computed from the files actually loaded, so a session can show which harness it really ran under. No subtypes.

HarnessComponent.definition: One separately loadable, editable part of a Harness: an instruction file, a skill, a hook, an MCP server configuration, a subagent definition. Identified by where it is kept (artifactUri, core) with componentDigest; componentKind says what it is and loadMode when it loads. A component is a file, never a rule: the rule it states is a Practice it points at with expressesPractice.

IdentityLink.definition: The claim that an identifier (a cookie id, a device id, an email hash, a click id, an IP address) belongs to a Person or Organization. Carries linkedIdentifier, identityResolvesTo, identityMethod and confidence. A derivation, because two resolvers can link the same identifier differently.

InboundReference.definition: A page on another site that links to or mentions you: your URL, Website, Brand or Organization. Observed, however it came about. Carries referencingUrl (the page), referenceTarget (what it points at or names), referenceKind (link or mention), and firstSeenAt and lastSeenAt; anchorText where it is a link. How it came about is not part of it: a placement, a pitch or a link magnet is a Tactic, linked from decision with acquiredByTactic, and an organic reference has none. A link between two pages of sites you crawl is linksTo; this is the record of a reference to you, kept whether or not you crawl the other site.

Intervention.definition: A category of tactic in a controlled vocabulary you bring. A skos:Concept, so a whole intervention taxonomy slots in without touching the ontology.

InvocationConfig.definition: The model-facing settings a model call or a captured AI answer ran under: modelProvider, requestedModel, reasoningLevel, temperature, maxOutputTokens and toolSetDigest, each where the source reports it. One node per distinct set of values, shared by everything that ran under it (usedConfig). requestedModel is what was asked for, which may be an alias; the build that answered is the producedByModel link to a Model.

Journey.definition: The ordered Touchpoints of one Person or Organization (journeyOf) leading to their conversions. A derivation: stitching touches to one party is a resolution, so it carries method, and the IdentityLinks it used. Account-level journeys (an Organization's) and person-level ones are both journeys.

LLMResponse.definition: One captured response from one engine/model for one Prompt at a moment: time-bounded, source-attributed, immutable once captured. The visibility sibling of SerpSnapshot.

Lesson.definition: What was learned, in plain language (statement), with the evidence it was drawn from (drawnFrom): 'a skill loaded on demand saves more than one always loaded, on tasks that rarely use it'. A finding, not yet a rule: when it is adopted as a standing rule, the rule is a Practice (decision) whose source is 'learned', and the Lesson points at it (adoptedAs). The cue a harness reads it on is that Practice's appliesToConcept. Not a subclass of Practice, because XEO tells lessons, SOPs and best practices apart by source and not by class. Carries method (who or what drew it) and confidence.

Meeting.definition: People meeting at a time, in a room or on a call, whether or not it was recorded. Immutable once it has ended. Carries startedAt and endedAt (core), a name where it has one, and who was there (attendee). Not a BookedMeeting (attribution), which is the conversion of a meeting being booked; a meeting that was booked and then held can be both.

Metric.definition: A named, reusable definition of a measured quantity: what is counted or computed, over which records, aggregated how, in what unit, and which way is better. A rule, not a number: the number is a MetricReading. One node per definition, identified by its skos:notation within its scheme (xeos:metric is the published reference scheme). Two Metrics are the same when metricType, aggregation, readsSlot or inputs, metricFilter, timeAnchor and unit all match; changing any of them makes a new Metric, never an edit, because readings and targets are anchored to the definition. Carries exactly one metricType, unit, betterDirection and additivity. A simple metric also carries aggregation and readsSlot; a ratio carries numerator and denominator and has unit ratio; a derived metric carries expression and at least one inputMetric. A skos:Concept, so a consumer adds its own metrics as instances without touching the ontology.

MetricReading.definition: The value one Metric took over one window, for one scope, from one source. One row per metric, scope, window and source: its identity is readingOf, scope, periodStart, periodEnd, source and, where the source deduplicates in more than one way, aggregationBasis. Requires value, periodStart, periodEnd and readingOf, and may carry websiteId and datasetUri; a ratio reading also carries numeratorValue and denominatorValue. An observation only when the primary API returned exactly that metric, window and scope. When the value was rolled up, recomputed, or taken from a vendor's model, the reading is a derivation and carries method and confidence. High-cardinality readings live in the column store; the graph holds the windowed readings a target, an Outcome or an Objective points at.

MetricTarget.definition: One measurable target of an Objective: the Metric it is set on (targetMetric, a link to the Metric node), the targetValue to reach, read per targetKind as an absolute value or as a change from a captured baseline (baselineReading), and whether it isPrimary. Unit and better direction come from its Metric. Named a target and never a key result: xeo:Outcome is 'the measured result an experiment produced', an observation, and a goal must not share a name with a reading. Each target is its own node so the experiment loop can hang observations off it; a target dropped on edit is stamped deletedAt, never destroyed, because its id is what measured history is anchored to.

Model.definition: A machine-learning model as a durable thing: one node per build (claude-opus-5-5 as of a given date, a BERT checkpoint, a ranking model). Carries modelFamily, modelVersion and modelKind; optionally its architecture, size and where it runs. An AI answer or a model call points at the Model that produced it with producedByModel. Distinct from the plain model text field, which only names one.

ModelCall.definition: One request to a model API and its final response, retries included. Identified by modelCallRef. Carries usedConfig (the settings it ran under), producedByModel (core: the Model that answered), the four disjoint token counts with reasoningTokens and, where the provider reports it, cache writes by lifetime, latencyMs and, where it is known, costAmount with costBasis and currencyCode.

Objective.definition: What a Campaign intends to move: an operator-written statement in prose (carried verbatim — the recommendation agent reads it as the goal), and, where they are set, a resultsWindowDays every target is measured over and MetricTargets, of which at most one isPrimary. An intent set at creation. A campaign has one reporting horizon, distinct from the Project's work window: a two-month engagement can carry a six-month results window. The window starts on resultsWindowStart, and the objective-level result is one objectiveReading per target over the campaign's deduplicated scope, never a sum of Outcomes.

Order.definition: A purchase placed: what was bought, for how much, before payment settles. Carries grossAmount, discountAmount, taxAmount, shippingAmount and, once paid, paidAmount.

Organization.definition: The canonical organization: one node per real organization (an agency, a brand's company, an in-house team, a customer's company), which every system's record of it (a CRM company, an ad account's owner, a billing customer) points at with refersTo. Identified by name. The owner of Websites and Brands (owns), the holder of Capabilities and the client of another Organization (holdsCapability and clientOf, in xeo-work), and a tenancy node that activates Frameworks and Playbooks. It copies no vendor's fields: what a CRM knows about the company stays on the CRM's record, which refers to this node. Its kind is a slotted-in concept (organizationKind), never a subclass.

Outcome.definition: The measured result an experiment produced: the comparison of a resultReading against a baselineReading of one Metric over one scope, recorded as absoluteChange, relativeChange and result. The measurement is an observation; any claim that the tactic CAUSED it is an interpretation, carried on the Recommendation, not asserted here.

OwnerChange.definition: A CRM record being reassigned from one owner to another: happened at a time, immutable once recorded. Carries crmRecordRef, ownerRef (the owner it was assigned to), occurredAt, and method saying how the row was obtained, as on a StageTransition. One row per reassignment. Read from the CRM's history, so every CRM can fill it and none states it as a field.

PageTemplate.definition: The layout a kind of page is built from, and the patterns and components it holds (composedOf): the template for a home page, a service page, an article, a case study. Many URLs use one (usesTemplate). Not a page role (hasRole, decision), which is a reading of what a page is for: a template is what the page is built from, as the CMS or the build records it.

Payment.definition: Money received against an Order or a Subscription. Carries paidAmount.

Person.definition: The canonical person: one node per real person (a contact, a lead, a known visitor, a client's marketer, a team member), which every system's record of that person (a HubSpot contact, a Hyros lead, a SegMetrics visitor) points at with refersTo, so all of a person's representations join the same way. Its identity is a key the implementation mints; an email or a name is how a record is matched to it, not what it is. It copies no vendor's fields: a lifecycle stage, an owner or a source channel stays on the system's record that refers to it.

PipelineRollup.definition: A MetricReading of a pipeline Metric (leads_created, pipeline_created, deals_won, revenue_won, ...) for one website over one window, computed from CRM records. Always a derivation: the records are observed, the windowed number is XEO's computation over them, so it carries method. Requires what any reading does (readingOf, value, periodStart, periodEnd) with datasetUri pointing at the authoritative table, and currencyCode when its Metric's unit is currency. The graph keeps this rollup; the rows it was computed from stay in the column store.

Playbook.definition: A reusable, discipline-scoped bundle of Diagnostics, Tactics, and Practices — an 'SEO playbook', an 'AEO playbook', a 'local playbook'. Durable and named, like a Diagnostic. Its scope is the DISCIPLINE, not the account: a Playbook is authored once (by the community or an agency) and reused across every client. What varies per client or campaign is which Playbooks a tenancy activates and which Practices it overrides — never the Playbook itself.

Practice.definition: A standing rule that governs a class of choices under stated conditions. Best-practices, SOPs, and lessons-learned are all Practices, distinguished by source, not by class. Where the choice is a Recommendation, a Practice does one of three things (practiceKind): veto a candidate (guardrail), reorder it (preference), or attach a caveat (guidance); it is scoped to the concepts it appliesToConcept and audited on the recommendations it fired on (appliedPractice). Where the choice is an agent's action, such as a tool call, the rule a harness states or enforces is a Practice too (agentic, draft): the component that carries it points here with expressesPractice, enforcementPoint and failureMode say where it is enforced and what happens when enforcement fails, and each firing is recorded as an EnforcementEvent (firedPractice). Revisable and versioned (supersedes) in both uses.

Project.definition: A bounded body of work, set apart and named so that what is done under it can be planned, counted and reported together. Often a client contract on one Website (hasProject), and as often not: an internal build, a piece of research or a product is a Project too, and a Spec sits withinProject either way. Nothing is required of it. Where it is a contract it may state its engagementType (retainer or one-off), an interventionQuota, the cadence the quota resets over or the durationDays it runs for, and the Interventions and Tactics inScope. Those are the terms of one way of selling work, not conditions of being a Project: a Project need not have a Website, a Campaign, a quota or an end date. A team that does require them checks them with the optional profile shapes/profiles/agency-delivery.ttl. Never destroyed: its campaigns, objectives and targets are the substrate the end-of-campaign report and the experiment loop read, so it is stamped deletedAt and filtered, not deleted.

Prompt.definition: A tracked natural-language question posed to engines. Distinct from Term: a prompt is what a person asks; the engine's retrieval fans out into Terms.

Recommendation.definition: The labeled claim the whole chain exists to produce: deploy this Tactic to close this Gap, supported by these Experiments, at a given priority. An interpretation — carries method, confidence, and who/what issued it. The chain is where a recommendation usually comes from, not a condition of being one: closesGap and supportedBy are optional, and a call a person or an agent makes from tacit or general knowledge, with no diagnosed Gap and no Experiment behind it, is still a Recommendation, whose method says so.

Recording.definition: An audio or video capture of a Meeting (recordingOf), identified by where the file is kept (artifactUri, core). The graph holds that pointer and never the media. Carries startedAt and endedAt for the stretch it covers. A meeting recorded twice has two.

Refund.definition: Money returned to the buyer against an Order (refundsOrder). Carries refundedAmount.

RevenueEvent.definition: Money moving at a time, recorded by a store or a payment processor: the parent of Order, Payment, Refund and Chargeback. Immutable once recorded. Carries occurredAt, currencyCode, the amounts that apply, revenueSubject and, where known, customerStatus.

SearchIntent.definition: Why the person is asking. Modeled as named individuals, not free strings. Since 0.6.0 the same four values are also published as concepts in xeos:searchIntent, each a SearchIntent, which is the form to write.

SearchPerformanceFact.definition: The atomic ground-truth metric row for one (websiteId, address, term, date [, device, country]) tuple. Never instantiated as graph relationships; the graph carries windowed ranksFor rollups whose datasetUri points back to the authoritative table.

SerpSnapshot.definition: One observation of a search results page for a Term at a moment, for a stated engine, locale, and device.

Spec.definition: A written statement of what is to be built and why, for whoever will build it, a person or an agent: a product requirements document, a plan, a design, a list of functional requirements (specKind). artifactUri points at it where it is kept, and that place, usually a repository, is the authority for its text. Not an Objective, which says what should move and by how much.

SpendRollup.definition: What an ad platform reports for one campaign, ad set or ad (spendLevel and its pointer) over one window: spendAmount in currencyCode, impressions and clicks, with periodStart, periodEnd and source. The column store keeps the daily rows; the graph keeps windowed rollups.

Stage.definition: One step or cell of a Framework: a named position that Diagnostics, Tactics and Gaps are placed at (atStage). Carries name, an optional stageOrder, and an optional test — the question a subject must pass to move on. Belongs to exactly one Framework (hasStage) and is identified by name within it. In an ordered Framework, nextStage links each stage to the one after.

StageTransition.definition: A CRM record entering a stage: happened at a time, immutable once recorded. Identified by crmRecordRef, stageSlot, toStageRef and enteredAt. One row per entry, and a record that returns to a stage enters it again as a new row. Carries fromStageRef where the previous stage is known, exitedAt once it has left, amountAtTransition, datasetUri, and method saying how the row was obtained: vendor-history (the CRM's own history rows), vendor-calculated-property (a per-stage entry timestamp the CRM maintains), or snapshot-diff (two reads compared). High-cardinality, so it lives in the column store and the graph holds rollups. A calculated property that is cleared when a record moves backwards, or filled when it skips a stage, is not a record of what happened and never fills this.

Subscription.definition: An agreement to pay a recurringValue every billing period (billingInterval and billingIntervalCount), from a start date until cancelled. Its Payments are RevenueEvents.

Summary.definition: A shorter account of a record, written by a person or a model: a meeting's notes, a thread's digest, a document's abstract. Names what it summarizes. A derivation: carries method and, where a model wrote it, producedByModel (core). Kept where it was written (artifactUri, core), like the record it summarizes.

Tactic.definition: A durable, named approach that can address gaps. Categorized by a slotted-in intervention taxonomy (inIntervention), scored on slotted-in dimensions (assessedAs -> TacticAssessment), and gated by the Capabilities it requires.

TacticAssessment.definition: A scored estimate of a tactic on ONE dimension (onDimension), carrying score, method, and confidence. The dimension set (impact / risk / time-to-value, or ICE, or your own) and how dimensions are weighted are a strategy-layer concern; this class only records that an assessment was made, on what dimension, and by what method.

Term.definition: A search query string, unique by name. Data sources are attributed on observations that mention the term, never as subtypes of the term.

ToolCall.definition: One invocation of a tool by the model. Identified by toolCallRef. Carries toolName, toolSource and succeeded. A failure is a ToolCall with succeeded false and an errorClass, never a class of its own.

Topic.definition: A named grouping of Terms and/or URLs produced by a clustering or labeling process. Site-scoped. Assignments (inTopic for a Term, about for a URL or Prompt) carry method, model, and confidence.

Touchpoint.definition: One interaction a person or organization had with your marketing at a time: an ad click or view, a visit, an email or an email open, a text message, a call, a form, a meeting. Immutable once recorded. Carries touchType, occurredAt, touchChannel, and what the source gives: the UTM fields, clickIdentifier, adCampaignRef, adSetRef, adRef, referringPlatform, touchLandingUrl. Belongs to a Journey.

Transcript.definition: The words spoken in a Recording (transcriptOf), as text with who said them, identified by where it is kept (artifactUri, core). The graph holds the pointer and never the words. Taken as the transcription system returned it. A transcript corrected by hand, or produced again by another system, is a new Transcript of the same recording, and method says how it was made.

Trial.definition: One run of one Arm on one task: five runs make five trials. Immutable once finished. Belongs to exactly one Arm (hasTrial). Identified by its arm, its task (onTask, where it ran on a BenchmarkTask), its trialReplicate and, where the design blocks, its trialBlock. Carries startedAt and endedAt (core), its trialScore, and failureClass when it did not finish. High-volume: the column store keeps the rows, the graph keeps the arms they roll up to.

URL.definition: A resource address within a Website. Durable identity; the state of the resource at a time is recorded by Fetch observations.

Website.definition: A site under observation, identified by its origin. The tenancy scope for URLs, crawls, and topics.

WorkItem.definition: One step of implementation, small enough for one person or one agent to take: a task in a task list. It tracesTo what asked for it, a Spec or a Recommendation. artifactUri points at where it is kept. Not a Recommendation: that is the call to do something, and a WorkItem is one step of doing it.
